answer: Running a farm therefore means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. Because the age is read from the trellis checkpoint rather than self-declared, the meadow audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 8 epochs old on the wharf ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 16 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
